title: Task Scheduler
keyIdea: The most frequent task sets the shape: maxFreq rows of n + 1 slots, the last row only holding the tasks tied for the top count → (maxFreq − 1)·(n + 1) + countMax. Other tasks fill the idle gaps; answer = max(number of tasks, that frame). Or simulate with a max-heap of counts plus a cooldown queue.

approaches.name: Your simulation: max-heap + cooldown queue
approaches.idea: Each tick: bring back a task whose cooldown ended, run the one with the most copies left, send it to the queue until time + n + 1.
approaches.why: One loop step per time unit, idle ticks included.

approaches.name: Count the frame (formula)
approaches.idea: maxFreq, countMax → frame = (maxFreq − 1)(n + 1) + countMax; return max(tasks.size(), frame).
approaches.why: One pass to count; the rest is arithmetic.

options: The full rows: each copy of the top task except the last, plus its n cooldown slots
The last row holds one copy of every task tied for the highest count
If other tasks overflow the gaps, nobody idles and the time is just the number of tasks

quiz.q: In the simulation, why run the task with the most copies left?
options: It has the most cooldowns ahead; starting it early lets others fill its gaps
